svg.title: From Korti to Khartum — The Desert March and the Ascent of the Nile, 1885
svg.text: The Desert March and the Ascent of the Nile in General Gordon’s Steamers
December 1884 – February 1885 · after the journal of Colonel Sir Charles W. Wilson
Stewart seizes the wells of Jakdul and returns to Korti.
The desert column leaves Korti; Wilson rides with Stewart.
Wells of Hambok and El Howeiyat.
Wells of Abu Halfa; Jakdul reached.
The column marches from Jakdul for Matammeh.
Battle of Abu Klea: the square is broken and re-formed.
Night march; action at Abu Kru. Stewart is wounded and
Wilson takes command. The column reaches the Nile at Gubat.
Attempt on Matammeh; Gordon’s steamers arrive.
Wilson sails for Khartum in the ‘Bordein’ and ‘Talahawiyeh’.
Khartum falls before daylight; Gordon is killed.
Through the Shabloka gorge, past Jebel Royan.
Off Khartum under heavy fire: no flag flies. The steamers turn back.
The ‘Talahawiyeh’ strikes a rock opposite Jebel Royan.
The ‘Bordein’ is wrecked near Wad Habashi; camp on Mernat.
Stuart-Wortley rows past the battery to Gubat for help.
Beresford’s ‘Es Safia’ engages the battery and brings the party
Wilson rides back across the desert to Korti.
Desert column, Korti to Gubat, 8–19 Jan. 1885
Detour by the wells of Abu Halfa and Jakdul
Route, camps, wells and dates after Wilson’s journal (Blackwood, 1885) and the sketch map published with it, set on a modern survey; positions in the desert are good to a few miles.

Relief: SRTM (NASA) via AWS Terrain Tiles. River: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. The Nile is drawn in its present course; the Merowe reservoir (2009) is omitted and the Fourth Cataract shown as open river.
